units.text: INT. DRIVE-IN PROJECTION BOOTH - NIGHT
Cramped.
Dust in the lamp beam.
A reel spins on its own.
Through the slit window: an empty lot, a flickering screen.
NELL AUGUSTINE, 20s, the projectionist, stands rigid.
Beside her, her brother SULLY, 16, holds a flashlight with both hands.
DOROTHEA "DOT" FEENEY, 60s, the owner, is wedged against the film cabinet, mouthing a prayer.
At the door, MR. KWABENA ASARE, 50s, a customer with a ruined suit, keeps one shoulder to the wood while a hand slams from the other side.
At the window, the booth's cat-eyed night guard BRYCE, 30s, whips the curtain shut, but a pale arm slides through the vent and clamps his ankle, dragging him down.
Dot! Dot, pull!
units.name: BRYCE

units.text: I'm pulling, Bryce, I'm pulling!
units.name: DOT

units.text: Sully swings the flashlight onto the arm.
Under the light, the skin peels like old film.
Nell, it's on the reel!
units.name: SULLY

units.text: Don't look at the screen!
units.name: NELL

units.text: Kwabena braces.
The door cracks.
Nell grabs the lamp housing and tears it open.
White light blasts into the vent.
The arm SCREAMS and lets go.
Silence.
The reel keeps spinning.
Is it gone?
units.name: KWABENA

units.text: On the screen, in huge flickering black and white, something turns toward the camera.
